results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

No pre-existing document specifically addressed User.password, @JsonIgnore, or WRITE_ONLY serialization. Using the API design guidelines (which establish the classification framework and breaking-change policy) as grounding, a new internal decision record DR-SEC-001 was composed. It records that @JsonIgnore on User.password is replaced by @JsonProperty(access = WRITE_ONLY), explains the rationale (identical response-hiding behavior, improved deserialization support, and better OpenAPI schema visibility), classifies the decision as 'internal', and summarises for the team that the change is non-breaking for consumers, maintains the security guarantee that passwords never appear in responses, and allows removal of previous deserialization workarounds.

output_document.summary: Decision record DR-SEC-001 (classification: internal) has been persisted to the project store. It records the team's decision to replace @JsonIgnore with @JsonProperty(access = JsonProperty.Access.WRITE_ONLY) on the User.password field. The change preserves the existing security guarantee — password hashes are never included in any JSON response — while also correctly permitting the field to be deserialized from inbound request bodies, closing a subtle silent-drop bug. No breaking change is introduced for API consumers. The record includes a before/after code snippet, a comparison table of the two annotations, and a clear action item for developers to adopt WRITE_ONLY as the standard pattern going forward.
